# Per-project idle-workbench report in the web console

## Description

Delivers an administrator-facing, per-project idle-workbench report in the
RHOAI web console. The report shows, for each workbench in a project, its last
activity timestamp, owner, and reserved resources (volumes and compute
reservations), sourced from the notebook controller's existing activity
tracking. This gives cluster administrators the visibility they need to
reclaim capacity from workbenches nobody has used in weeks. The epic also
delivers CSV export of this report.

The notebook controller requires no changes: it already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and this epic reads that data read-only from interfaces available
to the console. Consumption of the activity-tracking data doubles as
validation of that passive component.

## Scope

- New admin-facing report view in the web console, scoped per data science
  project, listing workbenches with:
  - last activity timestamp (from the notebook controller's activity tracking)
  - owner
  - reserved resources (storage volumes and compute reservations)
- Data sourcing in the console from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking and Notebook resources, read-only
- CSV export of the idle-workbench report
- Empty-state handling for projects with no idle workbenches
- Out of scope (per strategy): automated reclamation or deletion of idle
  resources; cost/chargeback calculations

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a data science project containing workbenches, when an administrator
  opens the idle-workbench report for that project, then every workbench is
  listed with its last activity timestamp, owner, and reserved resources,
  measured by agreement with the notebook controller's activity tracking data.
- Given a project with no idle workbenches, when the report is opened, then a
  clear empty state is shown.
- Given the idle-workbench report, when an administrator exports it as CSV,
  then a CSV file containing the displayed report rows (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) is produced and downloads successfully.
- The report is read-only: notebook-controller behavior and workbench state
  are not modified by viewing or exporting the report.
- The console's existing build pipeline and test suite remain green with the
  new report in place.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) sourced from notebook controller activity tracking.
- HLR-3 (P2): administrators can export the report as CSV (bundled here
  because it extends this report's own view and data).

# Stale pipeline-run report in the web console

## Description

Delivers an administrator-facing stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web
console. The report lists completed pipeline runs older than a configurable
age that still retain their artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines' run
completion metadata. This lets administrators see where old run artifacts are
accumulating storage so they can reclaim capacity with confidence. The epic
also delivers CSV export of this report.

Kubeflow Pipelines requires no changes: it already retains run completion
metadata, and this epic reads that metadata read-only from interfaces
available to the console (e.g. the pipelines API the console already
surfaces). Consumption of the run metadata doubles as validation of that
passive component.

## Scope

- New admin-facing report view in the web console listing completed pipeline
  runs, per project, that are older than a configurable age threshold and have
  retained artifacts, including:
  - run identification and completion timestamp (from KFP run metadata)
  - retained artifact indication / storage footprint information available
    from run metadata
- A configurable age threshold defining when a completed run counts as stale,
  with a sensible default
- CSV export of the stale pipeline-run report
- Empty-state handling for projects with no stale runs
- Out of scope (per strategy): automated reclamation or deletion of runs or
  artifacts; cost/chargeback calculations

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with completed pipeline runs, when an administrator opens
  the stale pipeline-run report, then completed runs older than the configured
  age with retained artifacts are listed, measured by agreement with
  Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Given the configurable age threshold, when an administrator changes it, then
  the report contents update to reflect the new threshold.
- Given a project with no stale runs, when the report is opened, then a clear
  empty state is shown.
- Given the stale pipeline-run report, when an administrator exports it as
  CSV, then a CSV file containing the displayed report rows is produced and
  downloads successfully.
- The report is read-only: pipeline runs and artifacts are not modified by
  viewing or exporting the report.
- The console's existing build pipeline and test suite remain green with the
  new report in place.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines
  run metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2): administrators can export the report as CSV (bundled here
  because it extends this report's own view and data).

# Documentation: idle resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

Authors product documentation for the two new console reports — the
per-project idle-workbench report and the stale pipeline-run report — and the
steps administrators can take to safely reclaim capacity from the resources
those reports surface. This is substantive new content (new documentation
topics), authored through the Red Hat docs content process once the reports
are implemented.

## Scope

Content outline:

- A documentation topic introducing idle resource reporting: what the reports
  are for and who they are for (cluster administrators)
- Reference documentation for each report:
  - idle-workbench report: where to find it, what each column means (last
    activity, owner, reserved resources), and where the data comes from
    (notebook controller activity tracking)
  - stale pipeline-run report: where to find it, what it lists (completed runs
    older than the configured age with retained artifacts), and how to
    configure the age threshold
- A how-to topic on safe reclamation steps: how administrators can manually
  stop/remove idle workbenches and clean up stale pipeline runs and their
  artifacts based on the reports, including cautions about data loss and
  verifying ownership before acting
- Explicit non-goals stated in docs where relevant: no automated reclamation,
  no cost/chargeback calculations

Out of scope: code changes of any kind.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation explains both the idle-workbench report and the stale
  pipeline-run report, including how to read them and how to configure the
  stale age threshold, measured by a reader being able to locate and interpret
  each report unaided.
- Documentation explains safe reclamation steps for idle workbenches and
  stale pipeline runs, with appropriate cautions.
- Content is technically reviewed against the implemented reports and matches
  actual product behavior (column names, data sources, configuration).
- Content passes through the Red Hat docs content process (technical review
  and editing) and is published.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps.
